name: San Diego
summary: A sunny Pacific port city on the Mexican border, known for its beaches, Balboa Park, the Navy, biotech on the Torrey Pines mesa, fish tacos and craft beer.

curated-2026-10.title: San Diego places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical 2025 asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for San Diego (Lindbergh Field)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals for San Diego International Airport (Lindbergh Field); the coast is cooler and inland neighborhoods warmer. Refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

climate.summary: Mild Mediterranean coastal climate: dry, sunny and warm most of the year, with short rainy winters and a gray marine layer ("May Gray" and "June Gloom") in late spring.

annual_events.summary: Big summer fair with rides, livestock and fried food at the Del Mar Fairgrounds north of the city.

annual_events.name: Comic-Con International
annual_events.summary: The huge pop culture convention takes over the Convention Center and the Gaslamp.

annual_events.name: San Diego Pride
annual_events.summary: Parade through Hillcrest and a festival in Balboa Park.

annual_events.name: Del Mar summer racing season
annual_events.summary: Thoroughbred racing at Del Mar, north of the city, opening with a famous hat-filled day.

annual_events.name: Little Italy Festa
annual_events.summary: Street festival with Italian food, music and chalk art.

annual_events.name: Fleet Week San Diego
annual_events.summary: Weeks of events honoring the armed forces around the bay; dates vary by year.

annual_events.name: December Nights
annual_events.summary: Free holiday festival with lights, food and music across Balboa Park.

annual_events.name: San Diego Bay Parade of Lights
annual_events.summary: Boats decorated with holiday lights parade around the bay.

annual_events.name: Holiday Bowl
annual_events.summary: College football bowl game, now played at Petco Park.

local_color.name: Fish tacos
local_color.summary: Baja-style fish tacos, battered and fried with shredded cabbage, white sauce and lime on a corn tortilla, are the city's signature cheap meal.

local_color.name: California burrito
local_color.summary: A San Diego invention: carne asada, French fries, cheese and guacamole or sour cream rolled in a flour tortilla.

local_color.name: Carne asada fries
local_color.summary: French fries buried under grilled steak, cheese, guacamole and sour cream, a late-night order after the bars close.

local_color.name: -berto's taco shops
local_color.summary: Cheap, often 24-hour taco shops whose names end in "-berto's" (Roberto's, Alberto's, Rigoberto's and many more) are on almost every main road.

local_color.name: May Gray and June Gloom
local_color.summary: In late spring and early summer a marine layer keeps the coast gray until midday or longer, to the surprise of visitors expecting sun.

local_color.name: Craft beer and IPAs
local_color.summary: San Diego has well over a hundred breweries and is known for hoppy West Coast IPAs; locals talk about breweries the way other cities talk about restaurants.

local_color.name: "The 5" and "the 8"
local_color.summary: Like the rest of Southern California, San Diegans put "the" in front of freeway numbers: take the 5 north, the 8 east, the 163 through Balboa Park.

local_color.name: OB and PB
local_color.summary: Ocean Beach and Pacific Beach are always "OB" and "PB"; OB is the laid-back, slightly hippie one and PB the party one.

local_color.name: Dawn patrol
local_color.summary: Surfer slang for paddling out at first light before work, when the wind is calm and the line-up is quiet.

local_color.name: Watching the sunset
local_color.summary: People stop what they are doing to watch the sun go down over the Pacific, with crowds gathering on the cliffs and piers on clear evenings.

local_color.name: Beach fire rings
local_color.summary: Concrete fire rings on some beaches are claimed early on summer weekends and holidays for bonfires, s'mores and evening gatherings.

local_color.name: Grunion runs
local_color.summary: On certain spring and summer nights after high tide, small silver grunion fish swarm onto the sand to spawn, and people come out with flashlights to watch.

local_color.name: Seal pupping season
local_color.summary: Harbor seals give birth on the Children's Pool beach in La Jolla, and the beach is closed to people from mid-December to mid-May.

local_color.name: Boba on Convoy
local_color.summary: Convoy Street in Kearny Mesa is the place for boba tea, ramen, Korean barbecue and late dinners from across Asia.

local_color.name: The Chargers left
local_color.summary: The NFL's Chargers played in San Diego for 56 years before moving to Los Angeles in 2017, and many locals are still bitter about it.

local_color.name: San Diego Padres
local_color.summary: The city's Major League Baseball team plays downtown at Petco Park in brown and gold, with a friar as its mascot.

local_color.name: San Diego Wave
local_color.summary: The NWSL women's soccer club, which has drawn some of the league's biggest crowds at Snapdragon Stadium since it began in 2022.

local_color.name: San Diego FC
local_color.summary: The city's Major League Soccer club, which began play in 2025 at Snapdragon Stadium.

local_color.name: SDSU Aztecs
local_color.summary: San Diego State's teams, with basketball at Viejas Arena and football at Snapdragon Stadium.
